- Context: MedScope will be evaluating a long-document summarization flow for clinical notes and imaging reports (average upload 18K tokens, 95th percentile ~45K).
- Primary goals: fidelity (no hallucinations on findings), consistent extractive Q&A for clinical review, and end-to-end latency for a single-doc summarization under 6s P95 if possible.
- Constraints: PHI-sensitive data; must run in VPC or Redwood Private for pilot if we progress.

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick reply with recommended starting configuration and links; I attached the prompt set and benchmark CSV for the tests we discussed. High-level:

1) Model recommendations (pilot):
   - redwood-long-64k-q4 (best for fidelity on long docs; quantized 4-bit, good tradeoff for cost).
   - redwood-realtime-extended-8k (fallback for low-latency single-pass summaries when document <8k tokens).

2) Eval harness & prompts: attached medscope_eval_prompts_v1.json — contains summarization templates, extractive Q&A pairs, and a short regression test set. Use the harness at the benchmark link below to run side-by-side comparisons.

3) Pilot plan (proposed):
   - Duration: 2 weeks
   - Scope: 500 redacted docs for fidelity checks + 1000 documents for latency sampling (mix of 2k/18k/45k token buckets).
   - Deliverables: summary fidelity report (ROUGE + clinical QA pass rates), per-token cost estimate, and recommended production config (caching/batching).

4) Ballpark cost: For a 2-week dedicated eval (private deployment, reserved capacity for the pilot): ~$14k–18k depending on dataset retention and VPC egress needs. We will send a formal SOW draft (attached).

Notes on truncation and mitigations:
- For docs >32k tokens we recommend either the 64k quantized model or a chunk+stitch strategy with a guided summarization prompt.
- Prefix/KV caching for recurring patient notes can reduce token throughput up to ~30% on stable sessions.

Subject: Re: Intro + long-context needs (follow-up) — technical observations

Soojin / Ben / Alina —

Looping in a few technical specifics from the runtime side that will matter for fidelity testing and which we should include in the test plan: 

1) Truncation failure modes we see in long-document summarization tests:
   - Edge hallucination: when relevant findings appear after the model's max KV window, summaries sometimes invent mild contextual content (~5–12% of samples above 40k tokens with base q4 behavior).
   - Loss of temporal ordering: multi-section clinical reports occasionally reorder events when the model processes chunked inputs without explicit boundary prompts.

2) Quantized perf notes (from internal runs against medscope-like docs):
   - redwood-long-64k-q4 shows stable QA F1 up to 48k tokens; beyond that we recommend explicit chunk-and-aggregate with a final guided re-summarization prompt.
   - In an internal test set (n=400), we observed a ~12% drop in extractive QA exact-match for quantized 4-bit models at token lengths >32k versus runs truncated at 16k. This is recoverable with block-level overlapping chunks (20% overlap) + final synthesis pass.

3) Recommended eval metrics and thresholds:
   - ROUGE-L, BLEU (low weight), extractive QA exact-match, clinician-rated hallucination score (0–3).
   - Target thresholds: QA exact-match >= 88% on redacted gold set; hallucination score <= 0.5 average.

4) Implementation suggestions (pilot):
   - Use redwood-long-64k-q4 as baseline for fidelity runs.
   - For production-mode latency-sensitive flows, model fallback to redwood-realtime-extended-8k depending on token histogram.
   - Cache patient prefixes (KV) for repeated note families; this reduces repeated prompt tokens when clinicians iterate.

Quick pseudocode for chunk+stitch pattern we recommend including in the harness: 

# PSEUDOCODE START
# input: long_doc (tokenized), chunk_size=8192, overlap=1638
chunks = []
for i in range(0, len(long_doc), chunk_size - overlap):
    chunks.append(long_doc[i:i+chunk_size])
partial_summaries = [model.summarize(c) for c in chunks]
final = model.summarize(
    "Given these partial summaries, produce a single concise clinical summary focusing on findings, dates, and recommendations: \n" + "\n".join(partial_summaries)
)
# PSEUDOCODE END

I'll attach a short SOW draft with required security controls for the Private pilot (VPC + KMS + audit logs).

—Marissa
